text:
Jen (AE): kicking off support swarm for Warden POC. Customer reported slow TTFT (600-900ms) vs our expectation ~150-200ms, and a few intermittent 429s. They also sent the security questionnaire (SOC2/KMS questions). tagging @Maria @Evan to triage.
Maria (SalesEng): thanks. can you drop a sample request/route and the env (hosted/dedicated)?
Jen (AE): hosted POC in us-west, default model variant. sample payload (redacted):
```json
{"prompt":"Summarize recent logs","max_tokens":150,"user_id":"warden-test-42"}
```
route header: `x-customer-id: warden-prod`

Evan (SRE): looking at the trace dump - :eyes: seeing repeated `kv_cache: miss` lines and long queueing in the shard queue. also batch windows frequently stretch to ~60ms for small requests which inflates TTFT. here's an excerpt of the debug log:
```
[2026-03-20T14:05:12Z] req=0x7f2b kv_cache=miss shard=5 queue_wait_ms=48 batch_window_ms=60 model_variant=redwood-small
[2026-03-20T14:05:12Z] req=0x7f2e kv_cache=miss shard=2 queue_wait_ms=52 batch_window_ms=62 model_variant=redwood-small
[2026-03-20T14:05:13Z] req=0x7f31 kv_cache=hit  shard=5 queue_wait_ms=10 batch_window_ms=12 model_variant=redwood-small
```

Sam (Runtime Eng): this looks like KV cache thrash + routing churn. customer is hitting many slightly different prefixes (they append metadata IDs in prompt) so cache keys don't match. also we saw cross-tenant routing flips — the request sometimes routes to a different shard which has a cold KV. two quick mitigations: 1) enable per-tenant cache pinning (sticky routing) for the POC; 2) reduce `batch_window_ms` for this route to 8-12ms so small requests don't wait for large batches.

Priya (Product): another angle — tokenization expansion. customer payload has un-normalized unicode and long UUIDs in prompt metadata which increases token count unexpectedly. if they normalize (NFKC) and strip debug IDs we can cut generated tokens and speed up KV hits. we can add a normalization hook in the request pipeline for the POC.

Maria (SalesEng): security questionnaire items: they asked about KMS/HSM and SOC2 status. Jen, do we have the SOC2 snapshot and KMS integration doc? ops-bot, can you attach the latest security pack?

ops-bot: attached -> https://internal.redwood/security/packs/soc2-2025.zip :white_check_mark:

finance-bot: Warden asked about trial credits vs reserved discount — they're interested in a short reserved commit if perf hits targets. rough discount band is 15-25% for a 3-6 month reserved pool.

Jen (AE): propose this plan: Maria will request customer to normalize prompts + remove debug IDs; Sam/Evan will enable sticky routing + reduce batch window on the canary route; Priya will push a normalization hook as a fallback; ops-bot attach SOC2/KMS docs; finance will propose a 3-month pilot discount. sound OK?

Evan (SRE): I'll run a controlled canary after config flips and post before/after metrics. expected improvement: TTFT down to ~180-240ms if cache hit rate goes up. queuing a run now, results in ~30m.

Sam (Runtime Eng): deploying sticky routing canary targeting only `warden-test-42` header. will post rollout progress and keep old route as fallback.

Maria (SalesEng): I'll coordinate with customer PM and security contact. will ask them to run sample batch of ~200 requests after changes.

Jen (AE): perfect. action items summarized:
- Jen/Maria: coordinate customer changes + collect sample payloads
- Sam: enable per-tenant cache pinning canary + reduce batch window
- Evan: run before/after perf test and upload trace
- Priya: add normalization hook as fallback
- ops-bot: attach SOC2/KMS docs (done)
- finance-bot: send pilot discount proposal

Jen (AE): tagging this thread for updates. will circle back with the customer once Evan posts results. :thumbsup:
